title: Constructible locus of failure of module stalk surjectivity
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, and $g:G\to F$ a morphism of constructible etale module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For $x\in X$ let $\bar x$ be the geometric point given by an algebraic closure of its residue field. Then $\{x\in X:g_{\bar x}:G_{\bar x}\to F_{\bar x}\text{ is not surjective}\}$ is a constructible subset [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Stalks are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks].

proof.text: Convert the constructibility predicates using isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff. Apply IsConstructibleSheaf.cokernel and convert back, obtaining a constructible cokernel C.

Apply constructibleEtaleModuleSupport to C, obtaining constructible support and independence of the zero-stalk condition from the chosen geometric point. At the canonical algebraic geometric point, PreservesCokernel.iso identifies the module stalk of C with the cokernel of the stalk map. The same stalk-colimit exactness instances used for abelian coefficients apply to ModuleCat. Preadditive.epi_iff_isZero_cokernel and ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective identify its vanishing with surjectivity.

Point.sheafFiberCompIso for forget₂ (ModuleCat Λ) AddCommGrpCat identifies the abelian stalk of the underlying cokernel with the underlying abelian group of its module stalk. AddCommGrpCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton and ModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton show their vanishing conditions coincide. A non-surjective canonical stalk gives a support witness. Conversely any nonzero support witness contradicts a surjective canonical stalk by independence of the geometric point. Thus the failure locus equals the constructible support.
